raw_response:
I've been growing cotton on this land for thirty years. My mother grew cotton here before me. I know this soil, I know these pests, I know when the rains come and when they don't. I don't need to overthink this — I do what works.

All 20 mu goes to cotton, same as every year. We only have two people in the house now, so I need a crop I can manage mostly alone, and cotton I know how to handle. I'll plant in late April after the last frost risk passes — around Grain Rain (谷雨). I've seen farmers rush and lose seedlings to cold snaps. I don't rush.

I'll buy hybrid seeds from the county seed station — the same kind I've used the last few years. They resist bollworm better than the old varieties. Not the cheapest, but I've learned the hard way that saving money on seed costs you more at harvest.

For fertilizer, I put down base fertilizer before planting — phosphorus and potassium worked in with tillage — then I top-dress nitrogen in two rounds: once when the plants branch out, once when bolls are setting. My neighbor uses less nitrogen but his plants look thin. I'd rather use a bit more and get full bolls.

My well gives me reliable water. I'll irrigate before planting to bring the soil up, then again at flowering and boll-set. If it's a dry summer like last year, I'll add one more round. Usually four times total.

Pesticides — I can't skip these. Bollworm, aphids, red spider mites, they come every year. I'll spray about six times, watching the plants carefully through the season. I start preventive spraying when I see the first signs.

I'll use rotary tillage before planting. It's what I always do. Breaks up the soil nicely for cotton roots.

I expect around 300 kg of seed cotton per mu if the summer isn't too extreme. Some years better, some worse. On 20 mu that's a decent income for two people.
